subproblems.title: Hausdorff-measure scaling under the blow-up map η_{x,r}
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, r > 0 and η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (Chapter03.blowUpMap x r); write Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Then for every set B ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} (no measurability assumed): (i) rⁿ·Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(B)) = Hⁿ(B) in [0, ∞]; (ii) the push-forward of the restricted measure Hⁿ⌞B under η_{x,r} equals rⁿ·(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(B)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (x : Amb n ℓ) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → ∀ B : Set (Amb n ℓ), ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) * (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' B) = (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) B ∧ ((μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict B).map (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r) = ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n) • (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)).restrict (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r '' B)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the scaling identity Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(A) for every set A. The Notation paragraph of the parent proof states it (“euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and translation invariance”). Here it is proved for arbitrary sets and upgraded to the push-forward form that the sibling children use for changes of variables. Throughout, n, ℓ, x, r > 0 and B are fixed, Hⁿ := μHE[n] and η := η_{x,r} = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r.
1. For every y, η(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) = r⁻¹y + (−r⁻¹x). Hence for every set S, η(S) = τ(r⁻¹S). Here r⁻¹S := {r⁻¹z : z ∈ S} is the pointwise scalar multiple (Set.image_smul; open scoped Pointwise) and τ(z) := z + (−r⁻¹x).
2. τ is an isometry of ℝ^{n+ℓ} (it is IsometryEquiv.addRight (−r⁻¹x)). So Hⁿ(τ(T)) = Hⁿ(T) for every set T (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, valid for arbitrary sets).
3. Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ with the nonzero scalar r⁻¹ gives Hⁿ(r⁻¹S) = ‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ·Hⁿ(S) for every set S.
4. In [0, ∞], ofReal(rⁿ)·‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ = 1: both factors are finite, and their product is the real number rⁿ·|r⁻¹|ⁿ = (r·r⁻¹)ⁿ = 1 because r > 0. Hence, by steps 1–3, ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ(η(S)) = ofReal(rⁿ)·‖r⁻¹‖₊ⁿ·Hⁿ(S) = Hⁿ(S) for every set S. Taking S := B proves (i).
5. η is continuous (an affine map), hence Borel measurable. It is injective: r⁻¹(a − x) = r⁻¹(b − x) forces a − x = b − x because r⁻¹ ≠ 0.
6. Let T be a Borel set. Since η⁻¹(T) is Borel, Measure.map_apply and Measure.restrict_apply give η_*(Hⁿ⌞B)(T) = (Hⁿ⌞B)(η⁻¹(T)) = Hⁿ(η⁻¹(T) ∩ B). On the other side, (ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ⌞η(B))(T) = ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ(T ∩ η(B)), and T ∩ η(B) = η(η⁻¹(T) ∩ B) (Set.image_inter_preimage). By step 4 applied to S := η⁻¹(T) ∩ B, ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ(η(η⁻¹(T) ∩ B)) = Hⁿ(η⁻¹(T) ∩ B). So both measures take the same value on every Borel set T and are equal (Measure.ext). This proves (ii).

η is continuous and injective

subproblems.title: Upper Density Theorem in μHE[n]-a.e. limit form (Simon 1.3.6)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ν any measure on (the Borel sets of) ℝ^{n+ℓ}, and A a Borel set with ν(A) < ∞. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A, ρ⁻ⁿ·ν(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Here B_ρ(x) is the closed ball and the quotient is taken in ℝ, i.e. it is (ρⁿ)⁻¹·ν.real(A ∩ B_ρ(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (A : Set (Amb n ℓ)), MeasurableSet A → ν A < ∞ → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)), x ∉ A → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ * ν.real (A ∩ closedBall x ρ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.6), which the parent proof invokes in steps 5(ii), 5(iii) and 6(a): “if ν is Borel regular and A is ν-measurable with ν(A) < ∞, then r⁻ⁿν(A ∩ B_r(x)) → 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A”. It is stated here once, in the exact form its two users need.
Tools: simongmt Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular, Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside (Simon 3.6 in a.e. form for simonHausdorffMeasureReal), Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Chapter02.simonAreaNormalization_eq_one, Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_pos and Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume_ne_top. The implementation may add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison` and `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLiteral`. Let ω_n := realUnitBallVolume (n : ℝ), which lies in (0, ∞).
1. The outer measure ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular in Simon's sense (measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular). The Borel set A is Carathéodory measurable for ν.toOuterMeasure (le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory ν A hA), and ν.toOuterMeasure(A) = ν(A) < ∞.
2. Apply Simon's Upper Density Theorem (ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside, with the real dimension (n : ℝ) ≥ 0). For simonHausdorffMeasureReal(n)-a.e. x, if x ∉ A then limsup_{ρ↓0} Q(ρ) = 0, where Q(ρ) := ν(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) / (ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ)) ∈ [0, ∞]. (Q is dimensionalDensityQuotient, and dimensionalUpperDensity is its limsup along 𝓝[>] 0.)
3. simonHausdorffMeasureReal(n) = simonAreaNormalization(n)•μHE[n] and simonAreaNormalization(n) = 1. So the statement of step 2 holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x.
4. Fix such an x with x ∉ A. Since 0 ≤ Q and limsup Q = 0 along 𝓝[>] 0, Q(ρ) → 0 (tendsto_of_le_liminf_of_limsup_le; the liminf is ≥ ⊥ = 0, and boundedness is automatic in [0, ∞]). As ω_n ≠ ∞, ω_n·Q(ρ) → ω_n·0 = 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). The limit 0 is finite, so (ω_n·Q(ρ)).toReal → 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal, ENNReal.toReal_zero).
5. Let ρ > 0, a := ν(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) and b := ofReal(ρ)ⁿ. First, ofReal(ρ)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(ρ)ⁿ (ENNReal.rpow_natCast). Next, ω_n·(a/(ω_n·b)) = a/b (mul_div_assoc, ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left with ω_n ≠ 0, ω_n ≠ ∞). Finally, (a/b).toReal = a.toReal/ρⁿ = (ρⁿ)⁻¹·ν.real(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) (ENNReal.toReal_div, ENNReal.toReal_pow, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal, Measure.real). Hence the two functions agree on (0, ∞), a set in 𝓝[>] 0. By step 4 and Tendsto.congr', (ρⁿ)⁻¹·ν.real(A ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A.

subproblems.title: Embedded C¹ submanifolds are Borel sets
subproblems.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^N satisfy IsC1Submanifold m S: each y ∈ S has open V ⊆ ℝᵐ, open W ∋ y and φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N that is C¹ and injective on V, with φ(V) = W ∩ S, V ∩ φ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dφ(v) injective for v ∈ V. Then S is a Borel (measurable) subset of ℝ^N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (S : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N))), IsC1Submanifold m S → MeasurableSet S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (“Each N_k is Borel: every y ∈ N_k has a chart (V, W, φ) with W ∩ N_k = φ(V), and φ(V) is closed in W because φ is continuous and proper into W; so N_k is locally closed, hence Borel”), with the details filled in. Fix m, N and S with IsC1Submanifold m S.
1. Charts. Fix y ∈ S. IsC1Submanifold m S gives open V ⊆ ℝᵐ and W ⊆ ℝ^N with y ∈ W, and φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N that is C¹ on V (in particular continuous on V). Moreover φ(V) = W ∩ S, and V ∩ φ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W.
2. Claim: W ∩ closure(S) ⊆ S. Let z ∈ W ∩ closure(S). As W is open, choose ε > 0 with B̆_ε(z) ⊆ W, and put K := B_{ε/2}(z) (closed ball). K is compact (ℝ^N is proper) and K ⊆ B̆_ε(z) ⊆ W. Hence Q := V ∩ φ⁻¹(K) is compact. φ is continuous on Q, so φ(Q) is compact and therefore closed. Also φ(Q) = φ(V) ∩ K = W ∩ S ∩ K (Set.image_inter_preimage).
3. z ∈ closure(W ∩ S ∩ K). Given δ > 0, since z ∈ closure(S) there is w ∈ S with ‖w − z‖ < min(δ, ε/2). Then w ∈ B̆_ε(z) ⊆ W and w ∈ K, so w ∈ W ∩ S ∩ K and ‖w − z‖ < δ. Since W ∩ S ∩ K = φ(Q) is closed, z ∈ φ(Q) ⊆ W ∩ S. In particular z ∈ S, which proves the claim of step 2.
4. For each y ∈ S, steps 1–3 give an open W_y with y ∈ W_y and W_y ∩ closure(S) ⊆ S. Let O := ⋃_{y ∈ S} W_y, an open set. Then S = O ∩ closure(S). If z ∈ S, then z ∈ W_z ⊆ O and z ∈ closure(S). Conversely, if z ∈ W_y ∩ closure(S) for some y ∈ S, then z ∈ S by the claim.
5. O is open and closure(S) is closed, so both are Borel. Hence S = O ∩ closure(S) is Borel (MeasurableSet).

z lies in the closure of W ∩ S ∩ K, so z ∈ S; hence W ∩ closure S ⊆ S

subproblems.title: A C¹ submanifold has an approximate tangent space at each of its points
subproblems.statement: Let m ≥ 1, N ∈ ℕ and S ⊆ ℝ^N with IsC1Submanifold m S. Then for every x ∈ S there is a linear subspace P of ℝ^N that is the approximate tangent space of S at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 with Hᵐ := μHE[m] (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m S x P). That is, finrank P = m and ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dHᵐ → ∫_P f dHᵐ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ). (P is the classical tangent space Dφ(v₀)(ℝᵐ) of any chart φ with φ(v₀) = x.)

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5(i), i.e. Simon's printed proof of Thm 3.1.6 “⇒”: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η_{x,r}(N_j)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{T_x N_j} f dHⁿ”. The proof uses the parent's method: a local injective C¹ parametrization of the submanifold near x, the area formula, and dominated convergence. The parametrization is the chart φ itself. The parent's graph map t ↦ x + t + w(t) is one particular injective C¹ parametrization of the same piece of the submanifold; using the chart directly removes the inverse-function-theorem step and leaves the area-formula and dominated-convergence argument unchanged.
Tools:
- The area formula simongmt Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea). Let s ⊆ ℝᵐ be measurable and ψ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N be injective on s and differentiable at every point of s with injective derivative. Then ∫_{ψ(s)} g dH^d = ∫_s J_ψ(u)·g(ψ(u)) dH^d(u) for every g : ℝ^N → ℝ, where d = finrank ℝ ℝᵐ = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin) and J_ψ(u) := Chapter02.areaJacobianAt ψ u = (fderiv ℝ ψ u).normDet ≥ 0.

Notation: Hᵐ := μHE[m] on ℝ^N and on ℝᵐ; η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x); B_ρ(p) is the closed ball and B̆_ρ(p) the open ball.
1. Chart and candidate plane. Fix x ∈ S. IsC1Submanifold m S at x gives open V ⊆ ℝᵐ, open W ⊆ ℝ^N with x ∈ W, and φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N that is C¹ on V and injective on V. Moreover φ(V) = W ∩ S, V ∩ φ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dφ(v) := fderiv ℝ φ v is injective for v ∈ V. As x ∈ W ∩ S = φ(V), pick v₀ ∈ V with φ(v₀) = x. Since V is open and φ is C¹ on V, φ is differentiable at every v ∈ V with derivative Dφ(v), and v ↦ Dφ(v) is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Let L := Dφ(v₀), an injective linear map, and P := L(ℝᵐ) = LinearMap.range L. Since L is injective, finrank P = m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ). It remains to show I(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f dHᵐ → ∫_P f dHᵐ as r ↓ 0.
2. Constants. Let M_f := sup|f| < ∞, and choose R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever ‖y‖ > R (tsupport f is compact). L is injective on the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ, so it is antilipschitz (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith): there is K > 0 with ‖u‖ ≤ K‖Lu‖. With c := 1/(2K) > 0, ‖Lu‖ ≥ 2c‖u‖ for all u. By continuity of Dφ at v₀ and openness of V, choose δ > 0 with B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V and ‖Dφ(v) − L‖ ≤ c for all v ∈ B_δ(v₀). Apply the mean value inequality on the convex set B_δ(v₀) (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le) to v ↦ φ(v) − L(v − v₀), whose derivative Dφ(v) − L has norm ≤ c. It gives ‖φ(v₀ + w) − x − Lw‖ ≤ c‖w‖ for ‖w‖ ≤ δ, hence
(a) ‖φ(v₀ + w) − x‖ ≥ 2c‖w‖ − c‖w‖ = c‖w‖ whenever ‖w‖ ≤ δ.
J_φ(v) := Dφ(v).normDet ≥ 0 is continuous on V (Dφ is continuous on V and normDet is continuous). B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V is compact, so there is Λ ≥ 0 with J_φ(v) ≤ Λ for all v ∈ B_δ(v₀) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn).
3. Separation. Choose ε₀ > 0 with B_{ε₀}(x) ⊆ W. K₀ := B_{ε₀}(x) is compact, so V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀) is compact, and Q := (V ∩ φ⁻¹(K₀)) ∖ B̆_δ(v₀) is compact (a closed subset of it). φ is continuous on Q. Also φ(v) ≠ x for v ∈ Q: otherwise φ(v) = φ(v₀), and injectivity on V gives v = v₀ ∈ B̆_δ(v₀). Hence ε₁ := min_{v ∈ Q} ‖φ(v) − x‖ > 0 if Q ≠ ∅. Let ε := min(ε₀, ε₁), or ε := ε₀ if Q = ∅. Then
(b) ‖φ(v) − x‖ ≥ ε for every v ∈ V with ‖v − v₀‖ ≥ δ.
Indeed, if φ(v) ∈ K₀ then v ∈ Q and ‖φ(v) − x‖ ≥ ε₁ ≥ ε; otherwise ‖φ(v) − x‖ > ε₀ ≥ ε.
4. Area formula. Fix r with 0 < r < ε/R. Put U_r := {u ∈ ℝᵐ : v₀ + ru ∈ V} (open, hence measurable) and ψ_r(u) := r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − x) = η_{x,r}(φ(v₀ + ru)). The map u ↦ v₀ + ru is a bijection of U_r onto V, so ψ_r(U_r) = η_{x,r}(φ(V)) = η_{x,r}(W ∩ S). Let B := B_R(0). Since f = 0 off B, f equals the indicator of B times f, so I(r) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B} f dHᵐ (setIntegral_indicator, B closed). If y = η_{x,r}(z) ∈ B with z ∈ S, then ‖z − x‖ = r‖y‖ ≤ rR < ε ≤ ε₀, so z ∈ W. Hence η_{x,r}(S) ∩ B = η_{x,r}(W ∩ S) ∩ B = ψ_r(U_r) ∩ B, and by the same indicator argument I(r) = ∫_{ψ_r(U_r)} f dHᵐ.
ψ_r is injective on U_r, because φ is injective on V. By the chain rule, ψ_r is differentiable at each u ∈ U_r with Dψ_r(u) = r⁻¹·Dφ(v₀ + ru)·r = Dφ(v₀ + ru), which is injective; so J_{ψ_r}(u) = J_φ(v₀ + ru). The area formula with s := U_r gives
I(r) = ∫_{U_r} J_φ(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)) dHᵐ(u) = ∫_{ℝᵐ} F_r dHᵐ, where F_r(u) := 1_{U_r}(u)·J_φ(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)).
Concretely: on U_r the area-formula integrand areaJacobianAt ψ_r u · f(ψ_r u) equals J_φ(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)) pointwise, so the set integrals over U_r agree (setIntegral_congr_fun, U_r measurable). Then integral_indicator turns ∫_{U_r} into ∫_{ℝᵐ} of the indicator.
Each F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable: it is the indicator of the open set U_r of a function that is continuous on U_r, because u ↦ v₀ + ru maps U_r into V, where φ and Dφ are continuous. Use ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable on U_r and aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff. Do not try to prove measurability of u ↦ f(ψ_r(u)) on all of ℝᵐ: φ is arbitrary off V.
5. Domination. Let 0 < r < ε/R and F_r(u) ≠ 0. Then v := v₀ + ru ∈ V and f(ψ_r(u)) ≠ 0, so ‖ψ_r(u)‖ ≤ R, i.e. ‖φ(v) − x‖ ≤ rR < ε. By (b), ‖ru‖ < δ. By (a), c·r‖u‖ ≤ ‖φ(v) − x‖ ≤ rR, so ‖u‖ ≤ R/c. Also J_φ(v) ≤ Λ since v ∈ B_δ(v₀). Hence |F_r(u)| ≤ G(u) := Λ·M_f·1_{B_{R/c}(0)}(u) for every u and every r ∈ (0, ε/R). G is Hᵐ-integrable on ℝᵐ, being bounded and supported in a compact ball.
6. Pointwise limit. Fix u ∈ ℝᵐ and let r ↓ 0. Since v₀ + ru → v₀ ∈ V and V is open, u ∈ U_r for all small r > 0, so F_r(u) eventually equals J_φ(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)) (pass to this function with Tendsto.congr'). J_φ(v₀ + ru) → J_φ(v₀) = J_L := L.normDet by continuity of Dφ at v₀ and of normDet. Also ψ_r(u) = r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)) → Lu, since φ has Fréchet derivative L at v₀ and the difference quotient along the direction u converges. Use HasFDerivAt.lim with the scaling r⁻¹ → ∞, or the one-variable derivative of t ↦ φ(v₀ + tu) at 0 restricted to t > 0; the case u = 0 is trivial. Hence f(ψ_r(u)) → f(Lu) by continuity of f, and F_r(u) → J_L·f(Lu).
7. Conclusion. The filter r ↓ 0 (𝓝[>] 0) is countably generated. So dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) with steps 4–6 gives I(r) = ∫ F_r dHᵐ → ∫_{ℝᵐ} J_L·f(Lu) dHᵐ(u). Apply the area formula to L itself with s := ℝᵐ: L is differentiable everywhere with derivative L, injective, and injective on ℝᵐ. It gives ∫_{ℝᵐ} J_L·f(Lu) dHᵐ(u) = ∫_{L(ℝᵐ)} f dHᵐ = ∫_P f dHᵐ. Since f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) was arbitrary and finrank P = m, P is the approximate tangent space: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m S x P.
proof_key_steps: chart (V, W, φ) at x and v₀ with φ(v₀) = x; L := Dφ(v₀) is injective, and P := L(ℝᵐ) has dimension m
lower bound ‖φ(v₀+w) − x‖ ≥ c‖w‖ on B_δ(v₀) by the mean value inequality, and a Jacobian bound Λ there
separation: ‖φ(v) − x‖ ≥ ε for v ∈ V outside B̆_δ(v₀), by compactness (properness) and injectivity
for r < ε/R, rewrite ∫_{η_{x,r}(S)} f as ∫_{U_r} J_φ(v₀+ru) f(ψ_r(u)) dHᵐ with ψ_r(u) = r⁻¹(φ(v₀+ru) − x), via the area formula
domination by Λ·sup|f|·1_{B_{R/c}(0)} and pointwise convergence to J_L f(Lu)
dominated convergence and the area formula for L give the limit ∫_P f dHᵐ

subproblems.title: Unweighted approximate tangent spaces a.e. on a finite-measure subset of a C¹ cover (Simon 3.1.6 ⇒)
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, ℓ ∈ ℕ and Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ}. Let C be a Borel set with Hⁿ(C) < ∞, Z a set with Hⁿ(Z) = 0, and (N_k)_{k∈ℕ} sets with IsC1Submanifold n (N_k) and Hⁿ(N_k) < ∞ for every k, such that C ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_k N_k. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ C there is a subspace P that is the approximate tangent space of C at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4 (Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (C Z : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (N : ℕ → Set (Amb n ℓ)), MeasurableSet C → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) C < ∞ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) Z = 0 → (∀ k, IsC1Submanifold n (N k) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (N k) < ∞) → C ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃ k, N k → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)), x ∈ C → ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x P
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon's printed proof of Thm 3.1.6 “⇒” together with Remark 3.1.3, as copied in steps 4–5 of the parent proof. It is specialised to a Borel set C of finite measure that is covered, up to the null set Z, by the given C¹ submanifolds of finite measure.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η := η_{x,r} (blowUpMap x r); T_x A = P abbreviates HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x P; B_ρ(p) is the closed ball; ν.real := (ν ·).toReal.
Siblings used:
- blowup_scaling (Submission.rsod_blowUpMap_measure_scaling).
- upper_density_zero (Submission.rsod_ae_tendsto_density_zero_outside): for every measure ν on ℝ^{n+ℓ} and every Borel S with ν(S) < ∞, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ S, (ρⁿ)⁻¹·ν.real(S ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
- c1_submanifold_measurable (Submission.rsod_isC1Submanifold_measurableSet) and c1_submanifold_tangent (Submission.rsod_isC1Submanifold_approxTangent), both used with N := n + ℓ.
1. Measurability and Remark 1.3. Each N_k is Borel by c1_submanifold_measurable. For k ∈ ℕ put C_k := (C ∩ N_k) ∖ ⋃_{i<k} N_i. Each C_k is Borel and C_k ⊆ C ∩ N_k. If x ∈ C ∖ Z, then x ∈ ⋃_k N_k because C ⊆ Z ∪ ⋃_k N_k, and for the least k with x ∈ N_k we get x ∈ C_k. Hence C ∖ Z ⊆ ⋃_k C_k.
2. Exceptional sets. Fix k and put A¹_k := C ∖ C_k and A²_k := N_k ∖ C_k. Both are Borel, with Hⁿ(A¹_k) ≤ Hⁿ(C) < ∞ and Hⁿ(A²_k) ≤ Hⁿ(N_k) < ∞. Apply upper_density_zero with ν := Hⁿ to S := A¹_k and to S := A²_k. This gives an Hⁿ-null set E_k such that for every x ∉ E_k and each i ∈ {1, 2} with x ∉ Aⁱ_k, (ρⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ.real(Aⁱ_k ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Every x ∈ C_k lies outside both A¹_k and A²_k.
3. Scaling facts. Let r > 0. For every set A, Hⁿ(η(A)) = (rⁿ)⁻¹Hⁿ(A) by part (i) of blowup_scaling (ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ(η(A)) = Hⁿ(A) with ofReal(rⁿ) ∈ (0, ∞)). For R > 0, η(A) ∩ B_R(0) = η(A ∩ B_{rR}(x)) because ‖η(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖. η is injective, and η(A) is the preimage of A under the continuous map y ↦ x + ry, so η(A) is Borel whenever A is.
4. Splitting (printed proof of 1.6 “⇒”). Fix k and x ∈ C_k ∖ E_k. Since x ∈ C_k ⊆ N_k, N_k satisfies IsC1Submanifold n, and n ≥ 1, c1_submanifold_tangent gives a subspace P with T_x N_k = P; in particular finrank P = n. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ), let M_f := sup|f|, and choose R > 0 with f = 0 off B_R(0). Let r > 0. By step 3, η(C) and η(N_k) have finite Hⁿ-measure. f is continuous and bounded by M_f, so f is integrable on each of them and on their subsets (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). η(C_k), η(A¹_k) and η(A²_k) are Borel. Since η is injective, C_k ⊆ C and C_k ⊆ N_k, η(C) is the disjoint union of η(C_k) and η(A¹_k), and η(N_k) is the disjoint union of η(C_k) and η(A²_k). Additivity of the integral over disjoint sets with the second set measurable (setIntegral_union) gives
∫_{η(C)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η(N_k)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η(A²_k)} f dHⁿ + ∫_{η(A¹_k)} f dHⁿ.
5. Error terms. Let i ∈ {1, 2}. Since f = 0 off B_R(0), ∫_{η(Aⁱ_k)} f = ∫_{η(Aⁱ_k) ∩ B_R(0)} f (setIntegral_indicator), and η(Aⁱ_k) ∩ B_R(0) has finite measure. So norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const and step 3 give
|∫_{η(Aⁱ_k)} f dHⁿ| ≤ M_f·Hⁿ.real(η(Aⁱ_k) ∩ B_R(0)) = M_f·Hⁿ.real(η(Aⁱ_k ∩ B_{rR}(x))) = M_f·(rⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ.real(Aⁱ_k ∩ B_{rR}(x)) = M_f·Rⁿ·((rR)ⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ.real(Aⁱ_k ∩ B_{rR}(x)).
As r ↓ 0, ρ := rR ↓ 0 (r ↦ rR maps 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0 because R > 0). So by step 2 (x ∈ C_k and x ∉ E_k) the right side tends to 0.
6. Main term and conclusion at x. ∫_{η(N_k)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ because T_x N_k = P. By steps 4–5, ∫_{η(C)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0. Since f was arbitrary and finrank P = n, T_x C = P. (This is Simon's Remark 1.5(2): T_x C = T_x N_k.)
7. Conclusion. Suppose x ∈ C has no approximate tangent space of C. Either x ∈ Z, or x ∈ C ∖ Z ⊆ ⋃_k C_k; in the latter case x ∈ C_k for some k, and then x ∈ E_k by step 6. Hence the exceptional set is contained in Z ∪ ⋃_k E_k, a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. So for Hⁿ-a.e. x, x ∈ C implies that some P satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x P.
proof_key_steps: each N_k is Borel (sibling); disjointify C_k := (C ∩ N_k) ∖ ⋃_{i<k} N_i, so that C ∖ Z ⊆ ⋃ C_k
the Upper Density Theorem (sibling upper_density_zero) for Hⁿ on C ∖ C_k and N_k ∖ C_k gives null sets E_k
each error term is ≤ sup|f|·Rⁿ·((rR)ⁿ)⁻¹·Hⁿ(A ∩ B_{rR}(x)) → 0, via blowup_scaling and zero density
the main term → ∫_P f with P = T_x N_k, from the sibling c1_submanifold_tangent
the exceptional set lies in Z ∪ ⋃ E_k, which is null

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces from unweighted ones on closed subsets (Simon Remark 3.1.8(1))
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^{n+ℓ}, A a Borel set with Hⁿ(A) < ∞, and ϑ : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ Borel measurable and Hⁿ-integrable on A. Suppose that for every closed set K ⊆ A, Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ K has an approximate tangent space of K (Simon Def. 3.1.4; Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P for some P). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A there is a subspace P that is the approximate tangent space of A at x with respect to ϑ (Simon Def. 3.1.7; Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A ϑ x P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (ϑ : Amb n ℓ → ℝ), MeasurableSet A → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) A < ∞ → Measurable ϑ → IntegrableOn ϑ A (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) → (∀ K : Set (Amb n ℓ), IsClosed K → K ⊆ A → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)), x ∈ K → ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)), x ∈ A → ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A ϑ x P
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon's Remark 3.1.8(1) (Lusin's theorem plus the Upper Density Theorem for the measure |ϑ|Hⁿ⌞A), in the detailed form of step 6 of the parent proof. The parent's “step 5 with C := C_i” is supplied here by the hypothesis of this statement.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η := η_{x,r} (blowUpMap x r); T_x K = P abbreviates HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n K x P; I_r(f) := ∫_{η(A)} f(y)·ϑ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y); B_ρ(p) is the closed ball; ν.real := (ν ·).toReal.
Siblings used:
- blowup_scaling (Submission.rsod_blowUpMap_measure_scaling).
- upper_density_zero (Submission.rsod_ae_tendsto_density_zero_outside): for every measure ν on ℝ^{n+ℓ} and every Borel S with ν(S) < ∞, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ S, (ρⁿ)⁻¹·ν.real(S ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
1. Lusin. Fix i ∈ ℕ. Apply simongmt Chapter01.IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.exists_isClosed_continuousOn (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 1.17; module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.Lusin) to the outer measure of Hⁿ, which is Borel regular (Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular). Its inputs:
- ClosedSetsAreGDelta for ℝ^{n+ℓ}: Chapter01.closedSetsAreGDelta_iff.mpr, since every closed set of a metric space is G_δ (IsClosed.isGδ).
- The Borel set A, which is Carathéodory measurable by le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory, with Hⁿ(A) < ∞.
- ϑ, measurable for the Carathéodory σ-algebra: ϑ is Borel measurable and Borel sets are Carathéodory measurable (apply le_toOuterMeasure_caratheodory to ϑ⁻¹(s) for Borel s ⊆ ℝ).
- ε := 1/(i+1) ≠ 0 in [0, ∞].
It gives a closed set C_i ⊆ A with Hⁿ(A ∖ C_i) < 1/(i+1) and ϑ continuous on C_i. Then Hⁿ(A ∖ ⋃_i C_i) ≤ Hⁿ(A ∖ C_j) < 1/(j+1) for every j, so Hⁿ(A ∖ ⋃_i C_i) = 0.
2. Weighted measure. Let μ' := (Hⁿ⌞A).withDensity(‖ϑ‖ₑ), i.e. μ'(S) = ∫_{S ∩ A} |ϑ| dHⁿ for Borel S. It is a finite measure because ϑ is integrable on A.
3. Exceptional sets. Fix i.
(a) Apply upper_density_zero with ν := μ' and the Borel set S := A ∖ C_i (μ'(S) ≤ μ'(univ) < ∞). It gives an Hⁿ-null set E'_i such that (ρⁿ)⁻¹·μ'.real((A ∖ C_i) ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 for every x ∉ (A ∖ C_i) ∪ E'_i.
(b) The hypothesis with the closed set K := C_i ⊆ A gives an Hⁿ-null set E''_i such that every x ∈ C_i ∖ E''_i has some P with T_x C_i = P.
Put E_i := E'_i ∪ E''_i.
4. Fix x ∈ C_i ∖ E_i and P with T_x C_i = P; in particular finrank P = n. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ), M_f := sup|f|, and R > 0 with f = 0 off B_R(0). It remains to show I_r(f) → ϑ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0.
5. Change of variables (blowup_scaling). Let r > 0. η is a measurable embedding, being an affine homeomorphism, e.g. (Homeomorph.subRight x).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ _); and x + rη(z) = z. For every set S, part (ii) gives η_*(Hⁿ⌞S) = ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ⌞η(S). Hence for every function F : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ (no measurability, sign or integrability needed), ∫_{η(S)} F(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_S F(z) dHⁿ(z) (integral_smul_measure and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). The same computation with lintegrals gives ∫⁻_{η(S)} G(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫⁻_S G dHⁿ for G ≥ 0, and integrability transfers (MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff, Integrable.smul_measure). Consequences:
(α) y ↦ f(y)ϑ(x + ry) is integrable on η(A). Indeed z ↦ f(η(z))ϑ(z) is integrable on A, being the product of the integrable ϑ with the bounded continuous f ∘ η (Integrable.bdd_mul), and integrability transfers along η.
(β) η(S) ∩ B_R(0) = η(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)) for every S, because ‖η(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖. So for Borel S ⊆ A, ∫_{η(S) ∩ B_R(0)} |ϑ(x + ry)| dHⁿ(y) = (rⁿ)⁻¹∫_{S ∩ B_{rR}(x)} |ϑ| dHⁿ = (rⁿ)⁻¹·μ'.real(S ∩ B_{rR}(x)).
(γ) Hⁿ(η(C_i)) = (rⁿ)⁻¹Hⁿ(C_i) < ∞ by part (i), so bounded Borel functions are integrable on η(C_i). η(C_i) and η(A ∖ C_i) are Borel (preimages of Borel sets under y ↦ x + ry) and disjoint (η is injective), and their union is η(A).
6. Bounded density ratio (Simon Remark 3.1.5(3)). Let g(y) := min(1, max(0, R + 1 − ‖y‖)). Then g ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ), 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g = 1 on B_R(0). By (γ), g is integrable on η(C_i), and Hⁿ.real(η(C_i) ∩ B_R(0)) = ∫_{η(C_i)} 1_{B_R(0)} dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{η(C_i)} g dHⁿ. Since T_x C_i = P, ∫_{η(C_i)} g dHⁿ → ∫_P g dHⁿ. So, eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, ∫_{η(C_i)} g dHⁿ ≤ Λ := ∫_P g dHⁿ + 1. By mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset there is r₁ > 0 with Hⁿ.real(η(C_i) ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ Λ for all 0 < r < r₁.
7. Splitting. By (α) and (γ) (setIntegral_union), I_r(f) = J₁(r) + J₂(r), with J₁(r) := ∫_{η(C_i)} f(y)ϑ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) and J₂(r) := ∫_{η(A ∖ C_i)} f(y)ϑ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y).
8. J₂(r) → 0. Since |f(y)ϑ(x + ry)| ≤ M_f·1_{B_R(0)}(y)·|ϑ(x + ry)|, (β) with S := A ∖ C_i gives |J₂(r)| ≤ M_f·(rⁿ)⁻¹·μ'.real((A ∖ C_i) ∩ B_{rR}(x)) = M_f·Rⁿ·((rR)ⁿ)⁻¹·μ'.real((A ∖ C_i) ∩ B_{rR}(x)). As r ↓ 0, ρ := rR ↓ 0. Since x ∈ C_i (so x ∉ A ∖ C_i) and x ∉ E'_i, step 3(a) gives |J₂(r)| → 0.
9. J₁(r) → ϑ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ. By (α) and (γ), J₁(r) − ϑ(x)∫_{η(C_i)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η(C_i)} f(y)(ϑ(x + ry) − ϑ(x)) dHⁿ(y). Let ε' > 0. Continuity of ϑ on C_i at x ∈ C_i gives δ > 0 with |ϑ(z) − ϑ(x)| < ε' for all z ∈ C_i with ‖z − x‖ < δ. Let 0 < r < min(r₁, δ/R). If y ∈ η(C_i) ∩ B_R(0), then z := x + ry ∈ C_i and ‖z − x‖ = r‖y‖ ≤ rR < δ; and f(y) = 0 for y ∉ B_R(0). Hence |J₁(r) − ϑ(x)∫_{η(C_i)} f dHⁿ| ≤ ε'·M_f·Hⁿ.real(η(C_i) ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ ε'·M_f·Λ. As ε' was arbitrary, J₁(r) − ϑ(x)∫_{η(C_i)} f dHⁿ → 0. Also ϑ(x)∫_{η(C_i)} f dHⁿ → ϑ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ because T_x C_i = P.
10. By steps 7–9, I_r(f) → ϑ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ. As f was arbitrary and finrank P = n, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A ϑ x P holds for every i and every x ∈ C_i ∖ E_i.
11. Conclusion. By steps 1 and 3, a point of A without a weighted approximate tangent space lies in (A ∖ ⋃_i C_i) ∪ ⋃_i E_i, a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x, x ∈ A implies that some P satisfies HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A ϑ x P.

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces depend only on the germ of (A, ϑ) at x modulo Hⁿ-null sets
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A A' O Z : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (ϑ ϑ' : Amb n ℓ → ℝ) (x : Amb n ℓ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) → IsOpen O → x ∈ O → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) Z = 0 → (A ∩ O) \ Z = (A' ∩ O) \ Z → (∀ z ∈ (A ∩ O) \ Z, ϑ z = ϑ' z) → ϑ x = ϑ' x → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A ϑ x P → Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A' ϑ' x P
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 (change of the weight on an Hⁿ-null set) and 3 (locality: only A near x matters) of the parent proof, merged into one statement. The hypothesis that A is Hⁿ-null-measurable makes the a.e. comparison of the integrands legitimate for the restricted measures.
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n]; η := η_{x,r} (blowUpMap x r). For a fixed test function f, I_r := ∫_{η(A)} f(y)ϑ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) and I'_r := ∫_{η(A')} f(y)ϑ'(x + ry) dHⁿ(y).
Sibling used: blowup_scaling (Submission.rsod_blowUpMap_measure_scaling), part (i).
1. Reduction. finrank P = n is part of the hypothesis. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^{n+ℓ}, ℝ). Choose R > 0 with f = 0 off B_R(0): tsupport f is compact, hence contained in some closed ball about 0, whose radius may be enlarged to be ≥ 1. Choose ρ > 0 with B̆_ρ(x) ⊆ O (O is open and x ∈ O). We show I_r = I'_r for every r ∈ (0, ρ/R). The interval (0, ρ/R) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), and I_r → ϑ(x)∫_P f dHⁿ = ϑ'(x)∫_P f dHⁿ by hypothesis. So it then follows that I'_r → ϑ'(x)∫_P f dHⁿ (Tendsto.congr'), which is the claim because f was arbitrary.
2. Fix r ∈ (0, ρ/R) and put B := B_R(0) and B_x := B_{rR}(x) (closed balls). Then rR < ρ, so B_x ⊆ B̆_ρ(x) ⊆ O. Since ‖η(z)‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖, η(S) ∩ B = η(S ∩ B_x) for every set S. Also x + rη(z) = z for every z, and η is injective.
3. Cut-off. For any ψ : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝ, the function y ↦ f(y)ψ(x + ry) vanishes off B, so it equals its indicator on the Borel set B. By setIntegral_indicator, for every set S, ∫_{η(S)} f(y)ψ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{η(S) ∩ B} f(y)ψ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{η(S ∩ B_x)} f(y)ψ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y). Hence I_r = ∫_s f(y)ϑ(x + ry) dHⁿ and I'_r = ∫_{s'} f(y)ϑ'(x + ry) dHⁿ, with s := η(A ∩ B_x) and s' := η(A' ∩ B_x).
4. η(Z) is null: by part (i) of blowup_scaling, ofReal(rⁿ)·Hⁿ(η(Z)) = Hⁿ(Z) = 0 and ofReal(rⁿ) ≠ 0, so Hⁿ(η(Z)) = 0.
5. s and s' agree up to η(Z). Let y ∈ s ∖ s' and write y = η(z) with z ∈ A ∩ B_x. If z ∉ Z, then z ∈ (A ∩ O) ∖ Z = (A' ∩ O) ∖ Z (because B_x ⊆ O), so z ∈ A' ∩ B_x and y ∈ s', a contradiction. Hence z ∈ Z and y ∈ η(Z). Symmetrically, using the hypothesis in the form (A' ∩ O) ∖ Z = (A ∩ O) ∖ Z, s' ∖ s ⊆ η(Z). By step 4, s and s' are Hⁿ-a.e. equal (ae_eq_set), so their set integrals coincide for every integrand (setIntegral_congr_set). Therefore I'_r = ∫_s f(y)ϑ'(x + ry) dHⁿ.
6. s is null-measurable. A ∩ B_x is null-measurable, so there is a Borel T ⊆ A ∩ B_x with Hⁿ((A ∩ B_x) ∖ T) = 0 (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). η is a measurable embedding ((Homeomorph.subRight x).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r⁻¹ _)), so η(T) is Borel. Hⁿ(η((A ∩ B_x) ∖ T)) = 0 by part (i) of blowup_scaling, and s = η(T) ∪ η((A ∩ B_x) ∖ T). Hence s is null-measurable.
7. Integrands agree a.e. on s. For Hⁿ-a.e. y we have y ∉ η(Z) (step 4). For such y with y ∈ s, write y = η(z) with z ∈ A ∩ B_x. Then z ∉ Z, so z ∈ (A ∩ O) ∖ Z and ϑ(z) = ϑ'(z) by hypothesis. As x + ry = z, f(y)ϑ(x + ry) = f(y)ϑ'(x + ry). Since s is null-measurable, setIntegral_congr_ae₀ gives ∫_s f(y)ϑ(x + ry) dHⁿ = ∫_s f(y)ϑ'(x + ry) dHⁿ; no integrability is needed.
8. By steps 3, 5 and 7, I_r = ∫_s fϑ(x + r·) = ∫_s fϑ'(x + r·) = I'_r for every r ∈ (0, ρ/R). This completes the proof by step 1.
